items.title: Pay 'processing fee' to release refund
items.quote: überweisen Sie bitte die einmalige Bearbeitungsgebühr von 49,90 € bis zum 27.11.2026 auf das Konto IBAN CY17 0020 0128 0000 0012 0052 7600.
items.computation: The letter states an explicit calendar date ('bis zum 27.11.2026') rather than a period to be calculated. As this is a private sender (not a German authority), no statutory delivery-fiction or §187/188 BGB counting applies; the date is used as printed. 27 Nov 2026 is a Friday, a normal working day in NW, so no weekend/holiday shift is needed even if it did apply.

warnings: This has the classic hallmarks of an advance-fee scam: you are asked to pay a 'processing fee' before receiving a promised refund — legitimate energy refunds never require the recipient to pay money first.
The payment IBAN (CY17...) is at a bank in Cyprus, not in Germany, which is highly unusual and suspicious for a supposed German consumer refund body.

The sender's address is in Nikosia, Cyprus, with no verifiable German corporate registration, yet it addresses a German consumer about German energy bills — sender identity does not match the claimed service.
The letter uses pressure tactics ('Verstreicht die Frist, verfällt Ihr Anspruch endgültig') to rush payment, a common scam technique.

There is no real company or authority named 'Verbraucher-Rückerstattungsstelle Energie' known to administer German energy cost refunds; do not send any money or personal/bank data, and do not click the email link — consider reporting this letter to the Verbraucherzentrale or police as suspected fraud instead of paying.
